studySystem.howToUse: ~2h theory + ~2h coding + ~1h project + ~1h revision + ~1h docs/interview. Shift flexibly on math/project-heavy days.
Use for durable fundamentals, mathematics and coherent explanations. Read selected chapters; do not attempt to finish every book.
Use as tutor, Socratic questioner, exercise generator, debugger, reviewer, architecture reviewer and mock interviewer—not as a code-copying shortcut.
Source of truth for current APIs, framework behavior, configuration and implementation details.
Approximately every 7 days. No major new topic. Work from blank files, retrieve concepts, debug deliberate failures, integrate multiple skills and record weak areas.
Every AI project should have a test set, explicit quality criteria, failure taxonomy and a repeatable regression check.
Spec → plan → context → implement → verify → review → approve. Keep permissions bounded and provide verifiers.
Problem → user → success metric → MVP → non-goals → architecture → build → measure → iterate.
Portfolio artifacts should include architecture, tests/evals, failure analysis, ADRs, security boundaries, cost/latency discussion and a clear demo.
